decisions.reason: This looks more like an incremental upgrade/repositioning of an existing trommel screen than a risky stand-alone launch, so performance aspirations are easier to meet and an established machinery firm would likely retain it.
A dedicated page and several models indicate strong commitment and expected market breadth, and with no clear sign of underperformance the firm would use its slack to continue the line.
Although only mentioned on the website, it fits the core mobile processing portfolio and a German machinery producer would usually allow more time for market learning before abandoning a new line.

The stationary electric fine shredder appears more niche and less prominently supported, but its fit with resource-saving recycling solutions makes near-term withdrawal still less likely than retention.

This green-waste grinder is somewhat narrowly targeted and only lightly evidenced on the website, yet it matches customer applications closely enough that management would probably keep it while evaluating demand.
A product line with its own page in a core stationary shredding segment suggests substantial commitment and acceptable early aspirations, so the firm would likely continue it.
